To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

for the elliptic cylinder, the most dangerous instability is when the cylinder is oscillating parallel to its minor axes and that the steady streaming flow is significantly affected by the instability for the circular cylinder.

the most dangerous configuration for any given eccentric cylinder is when it oscillates parallel to the minor axis and that the steady streaming of the basic flow, which is the flow that is generated when the oscillation is stopped, is significantly altered by this instability.

the stability of the flow induced by the oscillation of a circular cylinder in a viscious fluid is investigated and the major assumption is made that the oscillation is large in which the unsteady boundary is set up on it.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the stability of the boundary layer on an oscillating cylinder.
the study of the stability of the flow induced by a transverse oscillation of an elliptic cylinder.
the stability of the flow induced by the transverse oscillation of an elliptic cylinder in a viscously fluid.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the instability of a cylinder oscillating in a viscous flow is not a significant effect.

the unsteady boundary layers on oscillating cylinders are unstable to infinitesimal disturbances and the growth of the disturbances is such as to produce a steady streaming flow in the far wake of the cylinder which has the same qualitative characteristics as the basic flow.

for a cylinder oscillating in a fluid at a large frequency, instability occurs at a Reynolds number of the order of the square of the oscillation frequency, and the instability mechanism involves the steady streaming flow in the wake of the cylinder.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the instability of the unsteady flow is a very strong function of the oscillation frequency and that for the most dangerous configuration the instability is very weakly dependent on the eccentricity of the elliptic cylinder.

for a circular cylinder the instability is most dangerous when the cylinder oscillation is parallel to the cylinder axis and for an elliptic cylinder it is most dangerous when oscillation is parallel with the minor axis.
the stability of the flow is governed by a single dimensionless parameter, namely the Reynolds number based on the oscillation frequency and the cylinder diameter.
The main takeaway from our work is that

for a given eccentricity, a cylinder oscillating parallel to its minor axes is more unstable than a cylinder oscillating perpendicular to it, which is the opposite of the case for steady flow past elliptic cylinders.
the stability of the flow is determined by the shape of the cylinder and not by its size.

the instability of the boundary layer on an oscillating elliptic cylinder has a strong influence on the flow field and that the instability of a circular cylinder is a special case of this more general problem.
